title.narrative: Subnational Governance Program for Nepal - Phase 2

description.narrative: The Sub-National Governance Program Phase 2 will build on the progress of Phase 1 to establish better systems and processes to promote clarity of functions and responsibilities between the spheres of government. This will be achieved through evidence based policy support, dispute resolution and inclusive coordination and collaboration between different stakeholders. The program will support the development, implementation and consolidation of new policies, processes and management tools through consultative processes in selected sub-national governments. This will provide more inclusive and effective service delivery at the sub-national level, particularly to promote health and economic security, and contribute towards more stable federal governance in Nepal.

title.narrative: Subnational Governance Program Phase II Mid-Term Review

description.narrative: The Program provided technical support to Mithila Municipality in finalizing two important policies. The first policy focused on guidelines for registering and monitoring local health institutions, while the second policy outlined procedures for emergency health service management. These policies aimed to improve the municipality's overall health service management capabilities. The guidelines for local health institutions will ensure a systematic approach to overseeing their functioning and quality, while the procedures for emergency health services will establish efficient protocols and response mechanisms. These policies work together to enhance the municipality's ability to deliver effective and responsive health services to its residents.

The Subnational Governance Program (SNGP) assisted the Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration (MoFAGA) in drafting a bill on urban solid waste management. This bill aims to establish legal clarity regarding the roles and responsibilities of the three tiers of government in managing solid waste, which is a top priority for local governments. Once enacted, the bill is expected to provide a strong legal framework for effective urban solid waste management, promoting coordinated efforts and contributing to cleanliness, environmental sustainability, and public health.

The Subnational Governance Program (SNGP) continues to promote disability-inclusive governance in its six partner municipalities. Through a national umbrella organisation of 400 Organisations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs), SNGP supports local governments to legislate disability-friendly laws and policies, and advocates for greater awareness and sensitivity in development initiatives. The commitment of local governments to disability inclusive planning is reflected through their annual budget disbursements ranging from $20,000 to $45,000 during 2024-25. Some municipalities have constructed tactile pathways for people with low or no vision, while others have provided targeted income generation training for persons with disabilities (PwDs). Thanks to SNGP’s awareness raising activities, 332 PwDs were able to successfully access government allowances to support good living outcomes.

The Subnational Governance Program (SNGP) has strengthened local health governance in seven partner municipalities. Technical assistance provided by SNGP through Public Health Officers supported municipalities to draft and implement key health policies. This included the Sickle Cell Management Procedure, Pharmacy Guidelines, and Municipal Health Policy in partner local governments. It facilitated platforms for policy dialogues on Nepal’s health insurance system, and operational challenges, including learning and sharing across local governments in health governance. SNGP mobilised local organisations to engage with the communities to identify local health needs and concerns, including free workout centres, health insurance for vulnerable and marginalised groups, timely access to medicines and health workers’ training. Of the 260 health projects identified through citizen consultations in two provinces, 31 projects were integrated into municipal plans and budgets for 2024-25.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: The Subnational Governance Program (SNGP) supports local and provincial governments to strengthen their public financial management systems and address evolving issues on fiscal federalism. This year, it trained members of the Municipal Accounts Committee in over 60 local governments in Sudurpaschim province on issues such as financial oversight, audit review and corrective actions. It also supported them to develop working procedures and facilitate regular meetings to uphold fiscal discipline and address audit issues flagged by the Office of the Attorney General. To promote local economic growth, SNGP supported three partner local governments to develop and pilot a ‘Growth Hub’ model. Based on this success, SNGP will scale up this activity in Koshi Province.

The Subnational Governance Program continued to provide technical assistance to 27 government bodies to support implementation of roles and functions under the federal system. It included seven partner municipalities, six provincial governments, and 14 national institutions. Key interventions included drafting new and revising current laws and policies to ensure clarity and functionality of governance mechanisms. This included reviewing the overlaps in the scope of work of government institutions, amending the National Assembly’s Rules of Procedure, drafting Lumbini Province’s Mines and Minerals Management Bill, streamlining the local government performance assessment system. The program also supported 269 local civil society organisations to promote civic engagement in the municipal planning and budgeting process. Through consultations with local communities, they identified local issues to advocate for resource allocation with respective local governments. The program contributes to the institutionalisation of the federal system by strengthening inclusion, accountability and intergovernmental coordination across all levels of government.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: The Subnational Governance Program offered technical assistance to Bagmati Province in conducting a midterm review of its initial five-year periodic plan. This review evaluated the province's progress in attaining its development goals and presented recommendations for future policies and development strategies. The review report and recommendations, endorsed by the Provincial Government, will serve as a foundation for the formulation of the province's second five-year periodic plan (FY2023/24 to FY2027/28).

Through DFAT’s flagship Subnational Governance Program, 350 civil society organisations were supported to build their capacity to engage in government planning and budgeting at local levels, contributing to improved inclusive public service delivery in partner municipalities. Our support to enhance citizen engagement contributed to: budgets being allocated for 563 community-led initiatives and 149 health related programs; implementation of joint action plans on waste management; rehabilitation of water sources; and improved health services (eg availability of essential medicines) in remote areas for marginalised communities.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: Under DFAT’s Sub National Governance Program (SNGP), we provided technical assistance to Tansen Municipality to develop its Local Economic Development Plan, which outlines economic priorities and strategies to attract investment, create jobs, improve infrastructure, and foster economic diversification and sustainability. SNGP also aided Waling and Tansen Municipalities in crafting their Mid-Term Expenditure Frameworks, essential for effective budget planning and financial management. Additionally, it assisted Birendranagar municipality in formulating a Revenue Improvement Plan to boost revenue generation for development initiatives. ‍ Through SNGP, we facilitated partnerships between Invest & Infra, a Business Development Service (BDS) provider, and three municipalities—Waling, Damak, and Bhimeshwor—to promote local enterprises by providing BDS services to high-potential Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) within the municipality. The objective is to enable local governments to independently deliver these services, ensuring sustained success beyond Invest & Infra's direct support.

Under DFAT’s Subnational Governance Program, Australia funded and deployed public health officers in four municipalities in Nepal (Damak, Waling, Bhimeshwor and Tikapur) to enhance local health service delivery through technical support. ‍ Australia's support contributed to: (i) an action plan in Waling municipality to address procurement delays and staff shortages in the health sector; (ii) the development and adoption of a health policy in Damak municipality; and (iii) improved health sector governance through inclusive and evidence-based health programming across partner municipalities.
